title: Conjugacy classes of commuting nilpotents
abstract: We consider the space $\mathcal M_{q,n}$ of regular $q$-tuples of commuting nilpotent endomorphisms of $k^n$ modulo simultaneous conjugation. We show that $\mathcal M_{q,n}$ admits a natural homogeneous space structure, and that it is an affine space bundle over $\mathbb P^{q-1}$. A closer look at the homogeneous structure reveals that, over $\mathbb C$ and with respect to the complex topology, $\mathcal M_{q,n}$ is a smooth vector bundle over $\mathbb P^{q-1}$. We prove that, in this case, $\mathcal M_{q,n}$ is diffeomorphic to a direct sum of twisted tangent bundles. We also prove that $\mathcal M_{q,n}$ possesses a universal property and represents a functor of ideals, and use it to identify $\mathcal M_{q,n}$ with an open subscheme of a punctual Hilbert scheme. By using a result of A. Iarrobino, we show that $\mathcal M_{q,n} \to \mathbb P^{q-1}$ is not a vector bundle, hence giving a family of affine space bundles that are not vector bundles.
conventions: The base field $k$ is assumed to be algebraically closed. In Lean, use a variable `(k : Type*) [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k]`.
The vector space $V$ is $k^n$. Use `Fin n → k` or `EuclideanSpace k (Fin n)` depending on whether inner product structure is needed (usually not for algebraic parts).
The ring $A_{q,n}$ is defined as the quotient $k[x_1, \dots, x_q] / \mathfrak{m}_0^n$. In Lean, this is `MvPolynomial (Fin q) k ⧸ Ideal.span {p | p.totalDegree ≥ n}`.

The space $\mathcal{M}_{q,n}$ is the moduli space of regular $q$-tuples of commuting nilpotents modulo conjugation. It is constructed as the homogeneous space $\operatorname{Aut}(A_{q,n}) / G_1$, where $G_1$ is the stabilizer of the ideal $\mathfrak{q}_1 = \langle x_2, \dots, x_q \rangle$.

The group $\operatorname{GA}_{q,n}$ is the algebraic group of $k$-algebra automorphisms of $A_{q,n}$. In Lean, this is `Aut (RingHom) (A_{q,n})` equipped with the appropriate algebraic group structure.

The parabolic subgroup $P_1$ is the intersection of $\operatorname{GL}_q(k)$ (acting on the linear part of $A_{q,n}$) with $G_1$. It corresponds to the stabilizer of the line $\langle x_1 \rangle$ in the linear dual.
The group $\mathcal{I}_{q,n}$ is the kernel of the natural map $\operatorname{GA}_{q,n} \to \operatorname{GL}_q(k)$ induced by the action on $\mathfrak{m}/\mathfrak{m}^2$.

The punctual Hilbert scheme $\operatorname{Hilb}^n_{[0]} \mathbb{P}^q$ is the reduced fiber of the Hilbert-Chow morphism over the cycle $n \cdot [0]$. In Lean, this requires defining the Hilbert scheme of points and the Hilbert-Chow map.
Twisted tangent bundles $T_{\mathbb{P}^{q-1}}(+j)$ refer to the sheaf $T_{\mathbb{P}^{q-1}} \otimes \mathcal{O}(j)$. In the smooth category over $\mathbb{C}$, this is a smooth vector bundle.

The term 'regular' for a $q$-tuple $(N_1, \dots, N_q)$ means that the associated representation $\rho: A_{q,n} \to \operatorname{End}(V)$ satisfies $\rho(u^{n-1}) \neq 0$ for some $u \in \mathfrak{m}$.

items.tex: A representation $\rho$ is called {\it regular} if $\rho(u^{n-1}) \ne 0$ for some $u\in \mathfrak m$. It is said to be {\it cyclic} if there is a vector $v\in V$ such that $\rho(\Aqn).v=V.$

items.section: The Artinian algebra $\Aqn$ and its representations
items.tex: A $q$-tuple $(N_1, \dots, N_q)$ of commuting nilpotents in $\End(V)$ is said to be {\it regular} (resp. {\it cyclic}) if the corresponding representation $\rho : A_{q,n} \to \End(V)$ determined by $\rho(x_i) = N_i$ is regular (resp. cyclic).

items.section: The Artinian algebra $\Aqn$ and its representations
items.tex: Let $\rho$ and $\rho'$ be two cyclic representations of $\Aqn$. Then $V_{\rho}$ and $V_{\rho'}$ are isomorphic as $\Aqn$-modules if and only if $\mathcal{A}(\rho)= \mathcal{A}(\rho').$ The isomorphism classes of cyclic representations of $\Aqn$ are in bijective correspondence with ideals in $\Aqn$ of codimension $n$ and with the simultaneous conjugacy classes of ordered $q$-tuples of commuting nilpotents.

items.statement_en: Let $\rho$ and $\rho'$ be two cyclic representations of the Artinian algebra $A_{q,n}$. Then the associated modules $V_{\rho}$ and $V_{\rho'}$ are isomorphic as $A_{q,n}$-modules if and only if their annihilator ideals are equal, i.e., $\mathcal{A}(\rho) = \mathcal{A}(\rho')$. items.statement_en:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field, and let $A_{q,n} = k[x_1, \dots, x_q] / \mathfrak{m}_0^n$ be the truncated polynomial algebra. Let $(Z_1, \dots, Z_q)$ be a regular $q$-tuple of commuting nilpotent endomorphisms of a finite-dimensional $k$-vector space $V$, meaning that $Z_i^{n-1} \neq 0$ for some $i$. Then:
1. For any $j \in \{1, \dots, q\}$, $Z_j$ is a polynomial in $Z_i$.
2. If $\rho: A_{q,n} \to \operatorname{End}_k(V)$ is the representation associated to the tuple, then the image $\rho(A_{q,n})$ is isomorphic as a $k$-algebra to $k[z]/(z^n)$.

items.statement_en:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field. Let $A_{q,n} = k[x_1, \dots, x_q] / \mathfrak{m}_0^n$ be the truncated polynomial algebra, and let $\operatorname{GA}_{q,n}$ be its group of $k$-algebra automorphisms. Let $\mathcal{I}_{q,n}$ be the kernel of the natural map $\operatorname{GA}_{q,n} \to \operatorname{GL}_q(k)$ induced by the action on $\mathfrak{m}/\mathfrak{m}^2$. Let $G_1$ be the stabilizer of the ideal $\mathfrak{q}_1 = \langle x_2, \dots, x_q \rangle$ in $\operatorname{GA}_{q,n}$, and let $P_1$ be the intersection of $G_1$ with the image of $\operatorname{GL}_q(k)$ in $\operatorname{GA}_{q,n}$. Then there are isomorphisms of varieties:
$$ \operatorname{GA}_{q,n} \simeq \operatorname{GL}_q(k) \times \mathcal{I}_{q,n} $$
$$ G_1 \simeq P_1 \times (\mathcal{I}_{q,n} \cap G_1) $$
Moreover:
1. The groups $\mathcal{I}_{q,n}$ and $\mathcal{I}_{q,n} \cap G_1$ are unipotent. For each $j$, the subgroup $\mathcal{I}^j_{q,n}$ of elements reducing to the identity modulo $\mathfrak{m}^{j+2}$ is normal in $\operatorname{GA}_{q,n}$.
2. There is an isomorphism of additive group schemes $\mathcal{I}^j_{q,n}/\mathcal{I}^{j+1}_{q,n} \simeq (\mathfrak{m}^{j+2}/\mathfrak{m}^{j+3})^q$.
3. There are natural isomorphisms of varieties $\mathcal{I}_{q,n} \simeq (\mathfrak{m}^2)^q$ and $\mathcal{I}_{q,n} \cap G_1 \simeq \mathfrak{m}^2 \times (\mathfrak{q}_1\mathfrak{m})^{q-1}$.
4. The groups $\operatorname{GA}_{q,n}$ and $G_1$ are connected affine group schemes.
